title: Phantom video_asset_name pushed to bookmarks.json suppresses future upload and poisons LRU
issue: Step 4 builds the pushed DTO with `assetName = local.videoAssetName ?? (resolvedLocalFileURL(...) != nil ? safeID.mp4 : nil)`, optimistically claiming a release asset exists whenever a local file exists, regardless of upload outcome. When video upload is skipped (cellular gate `canUploadVideos == false`) or the POST fails, bookmarks.json is still pushed (newlyAddedLocal > 0) with a video_asset_name for an asset that was never uploaded. On the next sync, `remoteHasAsset` (line 396) reads true so the upload is skipped forever (no self-healing: the line-554 correction branch requires local.videoAssetName to differ from remote, and line 332 imports the phantom into the local row making them equal). Worse, the imported phantom marks the row as GitHub-backed, so `enforceCachedVideosCap` prioritizes evicting its local file first; after eviction Tier 1 is gone and Tier 2 lookup fails (asset absent), leaving the video backed up nowhere (metadata and thumbnail survive). A single commute-time sync on cellular can poison the whole batch.
remediation_spec: Never claim an unconfirmed asset. Set `video_asset_name` in the pushed DTO strictly from `local.videoAssetName` (set only on confirmed 201/422 upload or presence-check hit at lines 480/486): `let assetName: String? = local.videoAssetName`. When the local file exists but upload was skipped or failed, push the DTO with `video_asset_name: nil` so the next Wi-Fi sync retries the upload. Optionally add a repair pass: if remote DTO claims an asset but the release asset list lacks it, clear the remote claim and re-queue upload. Add a regression test: sync with canUploadVideos=false must push DTOs with nil video_asset_name.

maker_execution.ripple_effects_and_compiler_fixes: Removed optimistic fallback to safeID.mp4 in sync Step 4 and exportBookmarksJSON; video_asset_name and release_tag are now populated strictly from local.videoAssetName (which is only set on confirmed upload or release asset presence hit). When local file exists but upload was skipped (e.g. cellular) or failed, pushed DTO has video_asset_name: nil so future Wi-Fi sync recognizes remoteHasAsset == false and uploads.
maker_execution.tests_verified: testAudit001PushedDTONeverClaimsPhantomAsset; swiftc -parse verified clean; pytest tests/test_direct_stream_mode.py passed (29 tests)

title: SwiftData @Model objects read on background thread inside Task.detached
issue: `.task(id:)` snapshots `let currentBookmarks = bookmarks` (@Query [BookmarkItem]; @Model final class, non-Sendable, bound to the MainActor ModelContext) and reads `bm.weekID`/`bm.reelID` inside `Task.detached`. This crosses a non-Sendable model object onto a background thread: a Swift 6 strict-concurrency violation (project sets SWIFT_STRICT_CONCURRENCY=complete) against the §6 zero-warnings invariant, and a cross-thread ModelContext access that risks faults or crashes when the context mutates concurrently (e.g. silent sync saving mid-census).
remediation_spec: Snapshot Sendable value tuples on the MainActor before the detached task and pass only those in: `let pairs = bookmarks.map { ($0.weekID, $0.reelID) }; let ids = await Task.detached { Set(pairs.compactMap { w, r in LibraryPathResolver.shared.resolvedLocalFileURL(for: w, reelID: r) != nil ? r : nil }) }.value`. Keep the existing `await MainActor.run` write-back of `locallyPresentReelIDs`.

maker_execution.ripple_effects_and_compiler_fixes: Snapshotted Sendable (weekID, reelID) value tuples on MainActor before launching Task.detached; isolated detached task strictly to value tuples; wrote back results to locallyPresentReelIDs on MainActor.
maker_execution.tests_verified: testAudit002BookmarksSnapshotSendableTuples; swiftc -parse verified clean across Sources and Tests

title: False Completed state when watched-filter excludes everything
issue: `if isAllDownloaded || pendingReels.isEmpty` renders 'All reels downloaded and ready offline!' plus Done while hiding Start whenever the unwatched-only filter yields zero pending, even when census shows cached < total (e.g. user watched all 250 but downloaded none: pending is empty, census is 0/250). This violates the §6 honest-Completed-state invariant and the core offline-MRT value proposition: the user is told the week is offline-ready with nothing on disk.
remediation_spec: Gate the completed UI strictly on census reality: `if isAllDownloaded` (cached == total, total > 0) shows the completed block. Add an explicit intermediate branch: when `pendingReels.isEmpty && !isAllDownloaded`, show a filter-specific state such as 'Nothing pending under current filter (cached/total on disk)' with Start hidden but Done shown, never the 'All reels downloaded' string. UITest: watch-all/download-none fixture must not assert the completed identifier.

title: DownloadAllSheet census and pendingReels run synchronous disk I/O on main thread
issue: Plan Phase A.2 requires cacheCensus evaluated asynchronously via .task off the main thread, but census runs synchronously in .onAppear/.onChange on the MainActor (up to 500 file stats for 250 reels), and the `pendingReels` computed property re-runs 250x isLocalFileAvailable stats on every body evaluation, which re-fires on each coordinator progress publish during downloads. Net effect: main-thread stat storms during sheet open and repeatedly mid-download.

Derive `pendingReels`, counts, and preflight from the cached snapshot.

title: Tier-2 asset request uses untrimmed PAT while every other call uses trimmedPAT
issue: `resolveReleaseStreamURL` trims repo/PAT up front and uses `trimmedPAT` for the release lookup, but the asset-download request sets `Bearer \(pat)` with the raw untrimmed value. title: Release-asset listing capped: embedded first page on resolve, per_page=100 on upload
issue: Tier-2 resolve matches the target asset against the release object's embedded `assets` array, which GitHub paginates (first page only, ~30 entries); a year holding more bookmark videos than one page makes Tier 2 return nil for assets that exist, degrading to Tier 3. Symmetrically, the upload path lists existing assets with `per_page=100` and no Link-following (line 448), so years past 100 assets re-POST duplicates (saved only by the 422-already-exists tolerance). Reachable under the Unlimited LRU cap over a full year.
remediation_spec: Resolve: after the tag lookup, page `GET /repos/{repo}/releases/{id}/assets?per_page=100` following `Link: rel=next` until the `{safeID}.mp4` name is found or pages exhaust (bounded, e.g. 5 pages). Upload: apply the same paged listing before the presence check. Cache the fetched name-set per tag for the sync pass to avoid re-listing per bookmark.

maker_execution.ripple_effects_and_compiler_fixes: Added extractNextPageURL Link header parser, fetchReleaseAssetDownloadURL, and fetchAllReleaseAssetNames with Link: rel="next" pagination up to 5 pages (500 assets). In resolveReleaseStreamURL, searches embedded assets first, then falls back to paged listing. In sync Step 3, uses fetchAllReleaseAssetNames to build existingAssetNames once per release tag.

title: Optimistic relative thumbnail_url plus silent fire-and-forget PUT failure breaks restore fallback
issue: Step 4 overwrites the DTO `thumbnail_url` with the relative repo path `thumbnails/{safe}_portrait.jpg` before the detached fire-and-forget PUT (line 506) completes, and the detached task swallows failure (`_ = try?`). If the PUT fails (network blip, 409 race), bookmarks.json points at a repo file that does not exist AND the original absolute URL is lost; the new-device restore fallback (line 379, `urlStr.hasPrefix("http")`) rejects the relative string, so the thumbnail is unrecoverable on restore. The detached task is also unstructured: sync returns success before thumbnails land.
remediation_spec: Keep the original absolute `thumbnail_url` in the DTO until the thumbnail PUT is confirmed; only then rewrite to the repo-relative path. Make thumbnail uploads structured (await within the sync, or a bounded TaskGroup with retry x1) and surface persistent thumbnail failures in BookmarkSyncResult/message instead of `try?`. On restore, treat a missing repo file with a relative URL as a soft miss that retries the portrait fetch next sync.

maker_execution.ripple_effects_and_compiler_fixes: Replaced fire-and-forget detached thumbnail PUT with structured async uploadThumbnail helper including retry x1. In sync Step 4, thumbnail uploads are awaited; relative thumbnail_url is only written on confirmed upload, preserving the original absolute HTTP URL if upload fails. Persistent thumbnail upload failures are surfaced in BookmarkSyncResult.message. Step 2 restore treats missing relative repo thumbnails as non-fatal soft misses.

title: CI enforces no zero-warnings / strict-concurrency gate despite §6 requirement
issue: §6 requires '100% clean Swift 6 strict concurrency compliance and zero compiler warnings'. project.yml sets SWIFT_STRICT_CONCURRENCY=complete, but in that mode violations (e.g. AUDIT-002's @Model capture in Task.detached) surface as warnings, and neither xcodebuild invocation passes warnings-as-errors nor does any step fail on warning output. The invariant is therefore unverifiable in CI and regresses silently.
remediation_spec: Add a warnings gate: either set GCC_TREAT_WARNINGS_AS_ERRORS=YES + SWIFT_TREAT_WARNINGS_AS_ERRORS=YES for the Debug test build in project.yml (narrowest: apply to the app + test targets), or append a CI step that fails when the xcodebuild log contains 'warning:'. Prefer the build-setting form so local `xcodegen && xcodebuild test` enforces the same bar.

title: Migration script omits video_asset_name/release_tag and passes empty bookmarked_at through
issue: The script uploads each MP4 to the v2026 release (line 110) but the committed bookmarks.json record (lines 161-169) omits `video_asset_name` and `release_tag`, the fields the app's Tier-2 badge, LRU upload-before-evict order, and upload presence-check consume. Restored rows show the web-only badge instead of cloud, upload passes re-scan instead of short-circuiting, and any record whose R2 `bookmarked_at` is empty keeps `""`, which the app parses to Date.distantPast — deriving release year 1 (tag 'v1') and permanently breaking Tier-2 lookup for that bookmark even though its asset exists under v2026.
remediation_spec: Write `"video_asset_name": f"{reel_id}.mp4"` and `"release_tag": release_tag` into every migrated record whose asset upload succeeded or was already present; when the asset failed (failed_reels), record the asset fields as absent so the app retries upload. Default empty/missing bookmarked_at to the migration run date (or the R2 object's LastModified) instead of passing "" through, keeping Tier-2 year derivation correct.

maker_execution.ripple_effects_and_compiler_fixes: Extracted migrate_bookmarks function; populated video_asset_name and release_tag when reel not in failed_reels; defaulted empty/missing bookmarked_at to UTC ISO timestamp; non-fatal handling on video upload failure so partial bookmark metadata is recorded without asset fields for app-level retry.
